note: Iter 2 (v1.9.87): 30 -> 0 open. Every finding was fixed at its root cause; nothing is accepted. Two iter-1 verdicts were wrong and are corrected below (rpm_secureboot_patcher.c popen was injectable from RPM payload file names; HOME was not validated).

hard_fixes.fix: create_efuse_img wrote `losetup --show` output to the predictable /tmp/habv4-loop-<pid>.txt and re-read it; as root a planted symlink/file let another user choose loop_dev, which only had to start with '/' before going into ~10 single-quoted shell commands. Now the output is captured directly (no temp file) and parse_loop_device() accepts only /dev/loop<1-6 digits> and rebuilds the path from the parsed number. Verified end to end (loop attached, partitioned, formatted, detached).

check_certificate_expiry no longer runs `date -d` in a shell: openssl's notAfter is parsed in C (openssl_date_to_epoch, sscanf + timegm, strict format). Same truncation as the former $(( / 86400 )); 30-day cert -> 29 both ways.

rpm_validate_mok_package passed a vmlinuz-* name found inside the validated RPM into `sbverify '...'` via popen. Reproduced: an RPM containing boot/vmlinuz-x'$(touch PWNED)' executed the payload. Now glob() finds the kernel and run_argv_output() runs sbverify via fork/execvp with no shell; cpio gets --no-absolute-filenames. Correctly signed kernel still verifies (signature_valid=1). Supersedes the iter-1 FALSE-POSITIVE verdict for :110.

cfg.photon_dir was built from unvalidated $HOME and then interpolated into shell commands. The home dir now comes from getpwuid(geteuid()) (the effective user's home; /root for the documented root use) and is checked with validate_path_safe; --work-dir remains the override. Supersedes the iter-1 DESIGN-DECISION that HOME is operator-controlled.
Not logging: the gpg --gen-key batch file. Its text is a compile-time constant, now written with fputs of string-literal concatenation instead of a format string.

Added whitelist sanitizer on the openssl notAfter output before formatting it into a shell 'date -d' command. Reject any character outside [A-Za-z0-9 :+-.,] so a maliciously-crafted cert cannot inject shell syntax through the certificate's NotAfter field.
Same defensive whitelist sanitizer in habv4_common.c's check_certificate_expiry; rejects any char outside [A-Za-z0-9 :+-.,] before piping the openssl output into 'date -d'.
Replaced strcpy(file_pattern, last_slash + 1) with snprintf bounded by sizeof(file_pattern); also bounds-clamped the memcpy into dir_part so an oversized pattern can no longer overflow either buffer.
Same: strcpy(file_pattern, pattern) replaced with snprintf bounded by sizeof(file_pattern).

iter1_accepted_superseded.reason: GPG_KEY_EMAIL is a compile-time constant 'habv4-rpm@local' used only as the UID of the locally-generated RPM signing key. Not a credential.
Same: 'habv4-rpm@local' is the literal UID for the generated GPG key.

run_cmd() is the central system() wrapper. Snyk's flow shows env-var HOME -> cfg.photon_dir -> snprintf into cmd. HOME is operator-controlled (and this tool runs as root by design); all CLI inputs that compose cmd are pre-validated by validate_path_safe.
scripts/config kernel-config setter; arguments come from a fixed driver-to-kconfig table and the kernel_src path which is built from cfg.photon_dir (validated).
Internal kernel-build command; sources cfg.photon_dir which is HOME + validated release.
scripts/config command path; same internal kernel_src composition as 1590.
Internal build orchestration in the same kernel-build flow.
Same internal kernel-build pipeline; cfg.photon_dir + fixed templates.
popen() inside run_cmd_output is a generic helper; caller-side cmds are composed from mkdtemp paths and rpm filenames discovered via opendir+readdir, all on root-only paths.
'rm -rf <tmp_dir>' where tmp_dir is the mkdtemp result (/tmp/XXXXXX); no operator-controlled or attacker-controlled content.
spec_path is derived from cfg.photon_dir (HOME + validated release). Tool is a root CLI for building Photon ISOs; reading spec files from the operator's home is the documented contract.
Same: kernel source path under cfg.photon_dir/SPECS/linux/.
